questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I moved away from Germany when I was 14 years old, so the motivation of choosing Berlin as a destination was a personal reason to go back, but also get to know another institutions approach of history studies.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I liked it a low, but regarding everything with deadlines, and getting the right and enough etcs points and getting them transcripted to my studies  here has been causing endless sleepness nights and anxiety, and still is. It it the ongoing fear of having done sonething wrong, missing a signature, missing a deadline etc etc.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think it was easy for me, because I do speak the language, but imagine it difficult as a foreigner.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Workshops, and writing e-mails, but I did not use that regarding informations upon arrival.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very difficult, so I guess my only recommendations would be talking to people, reaching out, using socials etc. and WG.gesucht, and put some effort in writing applications

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It might be more difficult to find accommodations off campus, but personally I think it was worth it. It is easier to get in touch with locals. But is someones intention is to build a network with other students, and international students maybe there is no need to look for housing off campus

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Dont know if I am able to answer that, because the housing I had had nothing to do with the housing available to students,

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Super hard. The welcomine meeting for international students was one week before last call of choosing courses and I really wished that someone had told me when the course catalogue opened, cause not having a schedule done when I arrived triggered me so much. I had to watch youtube videos on how to register at the host institutions.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You find the different courses in the course catalogue, and put them together in your own schedule so they fit. Then you wait for acceptance/denial, but as a ERASMUS student you usually get accepted, which was super nice.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Writing e-mails or visiting the welcome meeting

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: very succesful, got all the courses I applied for

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: be patient and if you get denied just show up at the first class. A lot of students dobbel book their classes, in fear of getting denied so ususally there will be some open spaces anyways.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I loved that you can choose out of the entire course catalogue, and also had courses with for example gender studies and other studies. I also liked that they had so many interesting lectures, everyone could visit.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I did not realise that the one course I visited was a Master course until the teacher told me. But it definetly had some tighter requirements in the exam.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was more old school. No teacher ever presented a power point and you needed to attend. It was not allowed to had missing attendence, and everyone needed to make a presentation to get the studie points just so pass the course.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 2 semesters

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really liked an immigrant story, because almost all participant were exchange students so it was a very special atmosphere, and safe space. Also the class on european integration with a critical touch was super interesting, because everyone had a different approach on what it means to be EU citizen, and in my generation i never thought that being a part of the EU was anything else than a good thing. And that course definetly approach was very interesting.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Health insurance was super expensive. But i expirienced a lof of times that my blue eu card was not accepted.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: No expenses on books or public transport which was nice. But a semester fee needed to be paid every semester and that was about 500 euro.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: did not use any of them,but they do have an amazing canteen

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don´t know actually

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: did not use any, so can´t give any tips, sorry.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would definetly recommend all the different museums, that offer free entrees on the first sunday every month. Also a trip to potsdam a bit outside of Berlin is very nice

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it very easy, but that might be because I am german. But I definetly had to get used to the way people always a kind of distant in a negative way.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Not other than reaching out to people and use the offers they provide.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I kind of felt like people outside and on campus always expect the worst of you. Especially the teacher student relation was super weird, because on the one side they wanted to teach you something, but on the other they always made you feel like you needed to prove them that you deserved a spot in their class

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I definetly felt like their was a bigger sense for acitivism in a political way,

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- be patient with people not answering mails 
- learn german, it definitely makes some things easier 
- don´t bicycle

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No further information

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I do think that despite all the anxiety it causesd, it was nice when things finally fell into it´s place, other than that it definetly opneded my mind that there is more than live in Copenhagen. The world is bigger than that

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: meeting academic standards, having so many courses at once

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
